text:
Alex R.: Heads up — hitting networking limits when provisioning the new GPU fleet in us-west-2 (ENI secondary IPs + Elastic IPs). Lots of launches failing.
Sarah (infra): Which account and what's the exact error? I can open a support case.
Alex R.: Account 987654321098. Console error: "You have exceeded the maximum number of addresses allowed for your account in this region." EC2 agent: "Cannot assign more secondary addresses to ENI" on ~30% of starts.
Mike Nguyen: How many public IPv4s do we actually need for this rollout? If partners can go behind ALB/NAT we could avoid a huge EIP bump.
Alex R.: Short answer: partners require stable public IPv4 per instance for inbound connections. We need ~150 per-instance public IPv4s for the initial rollout. Current EIP quota in us-west-2 = 5.
Ira Patel: Alternatives: (1) Put instances private + NAT egress (cuts EIP need but inbound breaks), (2) dual-stack IPv6 for new fleet (longer path), (3) ALB with static frontend + internal targets (but doesn't give per-instance IPv4). Which is acceptable to partners?
Alex R.: They need per-instance IPv4 for now. Proposed immediate requests to AWS:
- Elastic IPs: 5 -> 200
- IPv4 secondary addresses per ENI: 30 -> 300
- ENIs per region: 50 -> 500
- VPCs per region: 5 -> 20
- Enable IPv6 dual-stack on the new VPCs as a fallback
Sarah (infra): I'll file the AWS support case and request TAM escalation. Any cost owner / charge code?
Alex R.: Chargecode INFRA-GPU. Launch target is Monday, please indicate urgency in the case.
Sarah (infra): Drafting case now. Copying body below for visibility:
-----
Subject: Urgent quota increases for Elastic IPs, ENIs, and secondary IPv4 addresses (Account 987654321098)

Account: 987654321098
Region: us-west-2
Requested increases:
- Elastic IPs: 5 -> 200
- IPv4 secondary addresses per ENI: 30 -> 300
- ENIs per region: 50 -> 500
- VPCs per region: 5 -> 20

Reason: Preparing dedicated GPU fleet (150+ instances) that require per-instance public IPv4 addresses for partner integrations. Time-sensitive, requested by 2026-03-23. Please escalate to account team/TAM and advise on subnet sizing and security review requirements.

Attachments: provisioning failure logs, launch template IDs, example error messages.
-----
Mike Nguyen: Add a request to scope EIP increase to a project tag or resource tag to speed approvals/security review.
Sarah (infra): Added tag scoping. Case created: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=case-0XABCDEF12
infra-bot: Support case case-0XABCDEF12 created by Sarah (infra) at 2026-03-18T14:35:10Z. Status: open.
AWS Support: We've received case-0XABCDEF12. We'll review quota limits and respond with ETA. May request additional justification for high ENI/secondary IP counts.
Ira Patel: When we get a tentative approval window, schedule a 15m runbook review to validate route tables, IGW limits, subnet CIDR sizing, and IPv6 prefix limits.
Alex R.: Agreed. @Sarah please share TAM contact when assigned and schedule runbook once we have an ETA. We'll also reduce per-instance secondary IPs temporarily and route non-inbound traffic via NAT so most instances can boot while EIP change is pending.
Mike Nguyen: Cost note: EIPs not attached to running instances incur charges. If we reserve 150 EIPs we should attach them immediately in provisioning to avoid waste.
Sarah (infra): Noted. We'll attach as part of the provisioning playbook. Also adding a mitigation: lower secondary IPs per ENI from 10 -> 2 for non-critical metrics to get boot parity.
AWS Support: Update: initial review complete. We may require a simple scaling plan showing steady growth and confirmation that addresses are for inbound services. Please upload the plan and confirm tag scoping.

Sarah (infra): Replying with scaling plan + screenshots of partner integration docs. Will post updates in this thread.
Alex R.: Thanks everyone. Once approved we'll run a dry provisioning pass with 20 instances to validate network attachments and the runbook. :thumbsup:
Mike Nguyen: Also consider enabling IPv6 early for new VPCs as longer-term mitigation. Add to runbook.
infra-bot: Case-0XABCDEF12 updated: AWS requested scaling plan. Sarah (infra) responded at 2026-03-18T15:02:34Z."
